title: Break a Palindrome
summary: Given a palindromic string of lowercase English letters, you are to replace exactly one character with any lowercase English letter so that the resulting string is no longer a palindrome.
statement: Given a palindromic string of lowercase English letters, you are to replace exactly one character with any lowercase English letter so that the resulting string is no longer a palindrome. The resulting string should be the lexicographically smallest possible. If it is impossible to make such a change, return an empty string. In lexicographical order, a string is considered smaller if, at the first position where it differs from another string, it contains a character that comes before the corresponding character in the other string.
constraints: Change exactly one character to obtain the lexicographically smallest non-palindrome, or empty string if impossible.
hints: A change in the first half dominates the mirrored position lexicographically.
Replace the first non-a before the midpoint with a.
If the first half is all a, change the final character to b; length one is impossible.
The earliest possible decrease is optimal, and the fallback makes the smallest possible increase latest.
editorial: The earliest possible decrease is optimal, and the fallback makes the smallest possible increase latest.

tests.explanation: Changing the first non-a in the first half to a produces aaccba.
Any one-character string remains a palindrome, so return empty.
